posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
We begin our journey into the question of what to do when life gives you lemons with the following poem from the 1940 edition of the Carnegian:

"Life handed him a lemon,
As Life sometimes will do.
His friends looked on in pity,
Assuming he was through.
They came upon him later,
Reclining in the shade
In calm contentment, drinking
A glass of lemonade."

Apt indeed, this is a variant on our standard wisdom, 'make lemonade'. There are, of course, other answers; our very own Scholar, for example, suggests a lemon cannon, while Cave Johnson of 2011's Portal offers a solution which demands to be quoted in full:

When life gives you lemons? Don't make lemonade. Make life take the lemons back! GET MAD! 'I don't want your damn lemons! What am I supposed to do with these?!' Demand to see life's manager! Make life rue the day it thought it could give Cave Johnson lemons! Do you know who I am?! I'm the man who's going to burn your house down! With the lemons! I'm going to get my engineers to invent a combustible lemon that burns your house down!

However, to find a true answer to our conundrum, I turn to personal experience and a message sent to me by a friend, apropos of nothing,two weeks ago, which read "When life hands you lemons just stay curled up in your ball of despair as the lemon pile consumes you entirely". This, evidently, is not the most optimistic of sentiments, and discussion soon got onto the various alternatives - for example, a lemon ball pit.

But none of those were the answer either; that comes two days later. Me and said friend took a train somewhere, and a drinks company were giving drinks away for some reason or other and gave her one. So, kids, don't worry about life giving you lemons - for sometimes life goes right ahead and gives you lemonade. The end.

posts.name: Bowie
posts.cooked:
I've met a lot of famous people. MOST Famous? Uhhhh... I ran into Natalie Portman at a Best Buy in LA, and almost lost my mind. I couldn't say a word, froze up and just stared. She smiled awkwardly and waved and said "Hello," noticing my clear starstruck appearance. This was a year after Phantom Menace, so she was pretty riding high on fame at the time. I think that might not constitute meeting.

For actual interactions, I hugged Rosario Dawson at a press tour she was on in Charlotte, NC when I was in the Army back in 2005, she smelled amazing.

That said, my favorite, I was in a hottub at the Atlanta Marriott for Dragoncon and Finn Jones and Kristian Nairn (Ser Loras Tyrell[Iron Fist now!] and Hodor of Game of Thrones) joined us. They were really nice. Finn had INFINITY questions to ask about America, because it was his first time visiting (Wrong Turn 5, which somehow I knew about, was brought up as a 'but you were in an American movie', to which he stunned me by telling me it was filmed in Bulgaria of all places.).

 

I’ve met a lot more than that, though. I’m from California and I’ve been deployed overseas, so both ‘big California cities’ celebrity meetings and ‘USO tours’ celebrity meetings are a thing I’ve known a good bit. Since then, I have become an avid costumer and do a lot of charity appearances and go to conventions around the country, so I end up meeting a lot of celebrities, from D-list to A-list (but mostly D).

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
The most famous person I've ever met would have to be Nobuo Uematsu.  I was working panels for Magfest (Music and gaming festival in maryland) and Nobuo was the featured guest.  He came because as a music and gaming festival he got to play a concert with his band and hang out as a musician.

His show was on Saturday night, and Sunday was teh end of the festival.  He had a Q&A session Sunday morning that was expected to be packed.  The weather was supposed to get bad, and everyone thought his session would be insane so it turned out that almost no one went.

There were about a dozen people there when it started, and by the end it got up to 30, in a room set up for 500.  He played music, talked with people, and it was an amazing time.

Here is a clip from his concert when he did the Magfest Colossus roar.  (it's from the X-men arcade game, and it caught on because you hear it so much in the big arcade game room)

Here is a clip from the interview session.  They had a translator, but for quite a bit this one person got to interview them in Japanese because there was no one there.  I can't find any that show the room, but in this one you can hear how incredibly quiet it was.

That's just some evidence.  The mess of water and candy dishes on the table were my friends responsibility, and he sat there giggling stupidly.

Anyway, I got into some of the conversation about composing on the old systems that he was having with the the guy who did the chiptune version of Nine inch Nails pretty little hate machine (which has fantastic stories behind it) and when he finally had to leave he shook my hand and said something in Japanese that I assume was a polite goodbye.

UXM266:

@Rabit: What movie, based on a comic book, would you like to see be made, and will it be animated, or live action?

This is surprisingly hard…

I mostly just watch live action, anymore, so animation is probably out. And almost everything I would have said (e.g., God Love, Man Kills; The Pheonix Saga; Days of Future Past; Spiderman No More; The Death of Gwyn Stacy; Kraven's Last Hunt; The Mutant Cure) has already been done poorly or bastardized. And honestly most of what I'd like to see them do, like good X-Men, New Mutant, Excaliber, DP-7, or Psi-Force stories, would actually require decent character development time, so they wouldn't really work as well as a movie – they really need to be a series.

So…

I guess it would have to be Freedom Four Annual #1 as a live-action movie. Yeah, that's the ticket.

I didn't know if they just were too embarassed to admit they didn't actually want it anymore or there was some other reason they hadn't been able to articulate. It felt very weird to me.
